cards.referenceTextZh: 将速度增加至 Mach 0.83 或更大，直飞 PEK，CES 769。

topics.name: CES 529 TCAS机动 备降/返航

cards.audioText: B: Your call sign is CES 529, you are maintaining 8400 meters, make an initial contact with Shanghai Control.
cards.audioTextZh: B：你的呼号是 CES 529，保持 8400 米，与上海管制首次联系。
cards.referenceText: Shanghai Control, CES 529, maintaining 8400 meters,.
cards.referenceTextZh: 上海管制，CES 529，保持 8400 米。

cards.audioText: CES 529, Shanghai Control, radar contact, climb to 10,400 meters.
cards.audioTextZh: CES 529，上海管制，雷达识别，爬升至 10,400 米。
cards.referenceText: climb to 10400 meters, CES 529. climb to 1400 meters, CES 529.
cards.referenceTextZh: 爬升至 10400 米，CES 529。爬升至 1400 米，CES 529。

cards.audioText: now you are cruising at 10,400 meters, your instruments indicate left pack has malfunctioned, contact Shanghai Control and request descend to lower levels.
cards.audioTextZh: 现在你正以 10,400 米巡航，仪表显示左组件故障，联系上海管制并请求下降至较低高度。
cards.referenceText: Shanghai Control, CES 529, maintaining 1400 meters, 10400 meters our instruments indicate left pack has malfunctioned, request descent to lower levels.
cards.referenceTextZh: 上海管制，CES 529，正保持 1400 米，10400 米，我们的仪表显示左组件故障，请求下降至较低高度。

cards.audioText: C: CES 529, turn right heading 240, descend to 8900 meters initially.
cards.audioTextZh: C：CES 529，右转航向 240，先下降至 8900 米。
cards.referenceText: Turn right heading 240, descend to 8900 meters initially, CES 529.
cards.referenceTextZh: 右转航向 240，先下降至 8900 米，CES 529。

cards.audioText: B: During descent, your right pack is overheating, both packs have malfunctioned and request emergency descent, this is a Distress call.
cards.audioTextZh: B：下降中，你的右组件过热，两个组件都故障，请求紧急下降，这是遇险呼叫。
cards.referenceText: MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY, Shanghai Control, CES 529, our right pack is overheating, both packs have malfunctioned, request emergency descent.
cards.referenceTextZh: MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY，上海管制，CES 529，我们的右组件过热，两个组件都故障，请求紧急下降。

cards.audioText: B: During descent, your cabin altitude is rising rapidly, request emergency descent to 3000 meters, this is a Distress call.
cards.audioTextZh: B：下降中，你的客舱高度快速上升，请求紧急下降至 3000 米，这是遇险呼叫。
cards.referenceText: MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY, Shanghai Control, CES 529, our cabin altitude is rising rapidly, request emergency descent to 3000 meters.
cards.referenceTextZh: MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY，上海管制，CES 529，我们的客舱高度快速上升，请求紧急下降至 3000 米。

cards.audioText: C: CES 529, descend to 3000 meters on QNH 1031.
cards.audioTextZh: C：CES 529，QNH 1031 下降至 3000 米。
cards.referenceText: Descend to 3000 meters on QNH 1031, CES 529.
cards.referenceTextZh: QNH 1031 下降至 3000 米，CES 529。

cards.audioText: B: Now you are maintaining 3000 meters, cabin altitude has resumed to normal, you will cancel Distress, report it to Shanghai Approach.
cards.audioTextZh: B：现在你保持 3000 米，客舱高度已恢复正常，你将取消遇险，向上海进近报告。
cards.referenceText: Shanghai Approach, CES 529, maintaining 3000 meters, the cabin altitude has resumed to normal, cancel Distress.
cards.referenceTextZh: 上海进近，CES 529，保持 3000 米，客舱高度已恢复正常，取消遇险。

cards.audioText: B: The cabin crew reports 5 passengers in the cabin are seriously injured during emergency descent, inform the situation to Shanghai Control and request diversion to Hangzhou.
cards.audioTextZh: B：客舱机组报告 5 名旅客在紧急下降中严重受伤，向上海管制通报情况并请求备降杭州。
cards.referenceText: Shanghai Control, CES 529, 5 passengers are seriously injured, request divert to Hangzhou.
cards.referenceTextZh: 上海管制，CES 529，5 名旅客严重受伤，请求备降杭州。

cards.audioText:
C: CES 529, divert to Hangzhou approved, what assistance do you need?
B: Tell the controller you need ambulances upon arrival.
cards.audioTextZh:
C：CES 529，同意备降杭州，你需要什么协助？
B：告诉管制员抵达时需要救护车。
cards.referenceText: Divert to Hangzhou approved, request ambulances upon arrival, CES 529.
cards.referenceTextZh: 同意备降杭州，请求抵达时救护车，CES 529。

cards.audioText: CES 529, roger, ambulance will be ready upon arrival.
cards.audioTextZh: CES 529，收到，救护车将在到达时就位。
cards.referenceText: roger, thanks, CES 529. CES 529
cards.referenceTextZh: 收到，谢谢，CES 529。CES 529。

cards.audioText: C: CES 529, turn right heading 180, descend and maintain 2100 meters, QNH 1031, expect ILS approach Runway 06.
cards.audioTextZh: C：CES 529，右转航向 180，下降并保持 2100 米，QNH 1031，预计 ILS 进近跑道 06。
cards.referenceText: Turn right heading 180, descend and maintain 2100 meters, QNH 1031, expect ILS approach Runway 06, CES 529.
cards.referenceTextZh: 右转航向 180，下降并保持 2100 米，QNH 1031，预计 ILS 进近跑道 06，CES 529。

cards.audioText: B: Now tell Hangzhou Tower about your situation and request priority landing.
cards.audioTextZh: B：现在告诉杭州塔台你的情况并请求优先着陆。
cards.referenceText: Hangzhou Tower, CES 529, 5 passengers were seriously injured during emergency descent, request priority landing.
cards.referenceTextZh: 杭州塔台，CES 529，5 名旅客在紧急下降中严重受伤，请求优先着陆。

cards.audioText: C: CES 529, straight ILS approach Runway 06, report established.
cards.audioTextZh: C：CES 529，直线 ILS 进近跑道 06，报告建立。
cards.referenceText: Straight ILS approach Runway 06, report established, CES 529.
cards.referenceTextZh: 直线 ILS 进近跑道 06，报告建立，CES 529。

cards.audioText: B: Now you have established on ILS approach Runway 06.
cards.audioTextZh: B：现在你已建立 ILS 进近跑道 06。
cards.referenceText: Hangzhou Tower, CES 529, established on ILS approach Runway 06.
cards.referenceTextZh: 杭州塔台，CES 529，已建立 ILS 进近跑道 06。

topics.name: CES 209 TCAS机动 备降/返航

cards.audioText: Your call sign is CES 209, you are in Shanghai Control area, you are maintaining 8400 meters, make an initial contact with Shanghai Control.
cards.audioTextZh: 你的呼号是 CES 209，你位于上海管制区，正保持 8400 米，与上海管制首次联系。
cards.referenceText: Shanghai Control, CES 209, maintaining 8400 meters.
cards.referenceTextZh: 上海管制，CES 209，正保持 8400 米。

cards.audioText: CES 209, Shanghai Control, radar contact, climb to 1400 meters.
cards.audioTextZh: CES 209，上海管制，雷达识别，爬升至 1400 米。
cards.referenceText: climb to 1400 meters, CES 209.
cards.referenceTextZh: 爬升至 1400 米，CES 209。

cards.audioText: now you are cruising at 1400 meters, your instruments indicate left pack has malfunctioned, contact Shanghai Control and request descend to lower levels.
cards.audioTextZh: 现在你正以 1400 米巡航，仪表显示左组件故障，联系上海管制并请求下降至较低高度。
cards.referenceText: Shanghai Control, CES 209, maintaining 1400 meters, 10400 meters our instruments indicate our left pack has malfunctioned, request descent to lower levels.
cards.referenceTextZh: 上海管制，CES 209，正保持 1400 米，10400 米，我们的仪表显示左组件故障，请求下降至较低高度。

cards.audioText: CES 209, turn right heading 240, descend to 8900 meters initially.

title: OPI
description: 发音 结构 词汇 流利度 理解能力 应对能力

cards.audioText: Have you ever encountered a lightning strike during flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中遇到过雷击吗？
cards.referenceText: One adjustable example is that I have not experienced a direct lightning strike in flight. I have operated near thunderstorms, so I treat lightning as part of a wider convective-weather threat. I would avoid the hazardous area rather than rely on the aircraft's lightning protection.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个可调整的示范答案是，我没有在飞行中遭遇过直接雷击。我曾在雷暴附近运行，因此会把雷电视为整个强对流天气威胁的一部分。我会避开危险区域，而不是依赖飞机的防雷保护。

cards.audioText: Under what weather conditions are lightning strikes most likely to occur?
cards.audioTextZh: 雷击最可能在哪些天气条件下发生？
cards.referenceText: Lightning is most likely in or near active convective clouds, especially thunderstorms with strong vertical development. Heavy precipitation, turbulence and electrical activity may occur in the same area. A pilot should use forecasts, reports and onboard weather information to avoid the whole hazardous cell.
cards.referenceTextZh: 雷电最可能出现在活跃的对流云内部或附近，尤其是垂直发展旺盛的雷暴中。同一区域还可能出现强降水、颠簸和电活动。飞行员应利用预报、报告和机载气象信息，避开整个危险单体。

cards.audioText: Why are lightning strikes hazardous to flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 为什么雷击会危及飞行安全？
cards.referenceText: A lightning strike can damage the skin, radome, antennas or electrical equipment. It may cause temporary instrument problems, system faults or a strong flash and noise that distract the crew. The surrounding thunderstorm can also bring severe turbulence, hail and icing, which may be a greater immediate threat.
cards.referenceTextZh: 雷击可能损坏机身蒙皮、雷达罩、天线或电气设备。它还可能引起短暂的仪表异常、系统故障，强烈的闪光和巨响也会分散机组注意力。雷暴本身还可能带来严重颠簸、冰雹和结冰，这些威胁在当时甚至可能更加紧迫。

cards.audioText: What should a pilot do if the aircraft is struck by lightning during flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中飞机遭遇雷击时，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: The crew should maintain control, confirm the flight path and check the aircraft for abnormal indications. They should follow the applicable checklist, assess the weather and system status, and advise ATC if a route change or priority is needed. A suitable landing and a maintenance inspection should be considered, especially if damage or a malfunction is suspected.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组应保持飞机受控，确认飞行轨迹，并检查是否有异常指示。随后应执行适用检查单，评估天气和系统状态；如果需要改变航路或获得优先保障，应通知 ATC。特别是在怀疑存在损伤或故障时，应考虑在合适的机场着陆并安排维修检查。

cards.audioText: What measures can pilots take to reduce the risk of a lightning strike?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行员可以采取哪些措施降低遭遇雷击的风险？
cards.referenceText: Pilots can reduce the risk by planning around convective weather and keeping a safe distance from thunderstorms. They should use current forecasts, weather radar, lightning information, pilot reports and ATC assistance without treating any one source as complete. If the safe route is uncertain, delaying, diverting or turning away is better than entering the cell.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员可以通过绕开对流天气进行航前规划，并与雷暴保持安全距离来降低风险。应综合使用现行预报、气象雷达、雷电信息、飞行员报告和 ATC 协助，而不能把任何单一信息源视为完整依据。如果无法确认航路安全，推迟起飞、备降或转向避让都比进入雷暴单体更好。

cards.audioText: What damage can a lightning strike cause to an aircraft?
cards.audioTextZh: 雷击会对飞机造成哪些损伤？
cards.referenceText: A strike may leave small burns, pits or holes at the entry and exit points. It can also damage composite material, the radome, lights, antennas, wiring or electronic systems. Some damage may not be visible during flight, so an inspection is important after a suspected strike.
cards.referenceTextZh: 雷击可能在雷击入口点和出口点留下小面积烧蚀、凹坑或孔洞。它还可能损坏复合材料、雷达罩、灯具、天线、线路或电子系统。有些损伤在飞行中不可见，因此疑似遭受雷击后进行检查很重要。

cards.audioText: During which phase of flight is an aircraft most likely to be struck by lightning?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞机在哪个飞行阶段最容易遭遇雷击？
cards.referenceText: Aircraft are most likely to be struck during the takeoff and landing parts of a flight, especially while climbing or descending through electrically active cloud. Strikes are less common in cruise because aircraft are often above the main cloud layer and crews have more opportunity to avoid storm cells. A strike can still occur in any phase when the aircraft is near active weather.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞机最可能在起飞和着陆相关阶段遭受雷击，尤其是在爬升或下降穿越电活动活跃的云层时。巡航阶段的雷击相对较少，因为飞机往往位于主要云层之上，而且机组有更多机会避开雷暴单体。不过，只要飞机接近活跃天气，任何飞行阶段都可能发生雷击。

cards.audioText: Have you ever encountered icing conditions during flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中遇到过结冰条件吗？
cards.referenceText: A sample pilot answer could be that I have encountered light icing conditions in cloud. The crew recognized the indications early, used the approved ice-protection systems and left the conditions. This is only an example; the actual response must follow the aircraft manual and company procedures.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个飞行员示范答案可以是：我曾在云中遇到轻度结冰条件。机组及早发现了相关迹象，使用经批准的防除冰系统，并离开了结冰条件。这只是示例；实际处置必须遵循飞机手册和公司程序。

cards.audioText: What cockpit or other indications can alert pilots to airframe icing?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪些驾驶舱指示或其他迹象可以提醒飞行员机体结冰？
cards.referenceText: Pilots may see ice on the windshield, wipers, wing areas, probes or other visible surfaces. An ice detector or caution may provide a direct indication on equipped aircraft. Unexpected loss of speed or performance, increased power demand, vibration or unusual control response can also suggest icing and requires prompt assessment.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员可能会在风挡、雨刷、机翼区域、探头或其他可见表面看到结冰。配备相应设备的飞机还可能通过结冰探测器或警戒信息直接提示。速度或性能意外下降、所需功率增大、振动或异常操纵反应，也可能表明出现结冰，需要迅速评估。

cards.audioText: How can in-flight icing affect flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 空中结冰会如何影响飞行安全？
cards.referenceText: Ice disturbs airflow, reduces lift and increases drag and weight. It can raise stall speed, reduce climb performance and affect handling, propulsion or sensors. Severe contamination may make the aircraft difficult or impossible to control, so early recognition and exit are essential.
cards.referenceTextZh: 结冰会扰乱气流、减小升力，并增大阻力和重量。它会提高失速速度、降低爬升性能，还可能影响操纵、推进系统或传感器。严重污染可能使飞机难以甚至无法控制，因此必须及早发现并离开结冰条件。

cards.audioText: What should pilots do if they encounter icing conditions in flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中遇到结冰条件时，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: The crew should use the approved ice-protection systems and follow the aircraft checklist. They should leave the icing conditions promptly by changing route or altitude as conditions and clearances permit, while maintaining safe speed and configuration. They should inform ATC when assistance is needed and report significant icing in accordance with applicable procedures.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组应使用经批准的防除冰系统，并执行飞机检查单。在条件和管制许可允许的情况下，应通过改变航路或高度迅速离开结冰区域，同时保持安全速度和构型。需要协助时应通知 ATC，并按照适用程序报告明显结冰。

cards.audioText: What should a pilot do if ice begins to accumulate on the wings in flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中机翼开始积冰时，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: The pilot should treat visible wing accumulation as a serious warning and apply the approved icing procedure. The crew should use the installed protection correctly, maintain the prescribed airspeed or required speed margin, and exit the conditions without delay. They should not improvise flap, autopilot or deicing actions outside the aircraft guidance.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应把可见的机翼积冰视为严重警告，并执行经批准的结冰处置程序。机组应正确使用已安装的防护系统，保持规定空速或所需速度裕度，并立即离开结冰条件。不得超出机型指导擅自操作襟翼、自动驾驶或除冰系统。

cards.audioText: Under what atmospheric conditions is aircraft icing likely to occur?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪些大气条件下容易发生飞机结冰？
cards.referenceText: Aircraft icing is likely when visible moisture is present and the temperature is cold enough for supercooled water to freeze on the aircraft. Clouds, freezing precipitation and some forms of drizzle or rain can create the hazard. The aircraft manual and current weather products should be used because the exact icing envelope and severity are not defined by one simple temperature value.
cards.referenceTextZh: 当存在可见水汽且温度低到足以使过冷水滴冻结在飞机上时，就容易出现飞机结冰。云、冻降水以及某些形式的毛毛雨或降雨都可能形成这种危险。由于准确的结冰范围和严重程度不能只用一个简单温度值界定，机组应参考飞机手册和现行气象产品。

cards.audioText: On which parts of an aircraft is ice most likely to form?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞机哪些部位最容易结冰？
cards.referenceText: Ice commonly forms on exposed leading edges and other surfaces that meet supercooled droplets first. These may include the wings, tail, propellers, engine inlets, windshield, antennas and probes. Ice can also form beyond protected or easily visible areas, so crews must not rely on one observation point alone.
cards.referenceTextZh: 结冰通常形成在暴露的前缘以及最先接触过冷水滴的其他表面。这些部位可能包括机翼、尾翼、螺旋桨、发动机进气口、风挡、天线和探头。冰还可能形成在防护区域之外或不易观察的位置，因此机组不能只依赖一个观察点。

cards.audioText: What de-icing systems are installed on the aircraft you fly?
cards.audioTextZh: 你所飞的飞机安装了哪些除冰系统？
cards.referenceText: A suitable aircraft-specific example would include pneumatic boots on selected leading edges and electrically heated probes and windshield areas. The propeller or engine inlet might use electric heat, fluid or heated air depending on the design. A learner should replace this example with the systems and limitations of the aircraft actually flown.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的机型示范答案可以包括：部分前缘使用气动除冰套，探头和部分风挡区域采用电加热。螺旋桨或发动机进气口则可能根据设计采用电加热、液体或热空气。学习者应根据自己实际飞行的飞机，替换为相应系统和限制。

cards.audioText: How does an aircraft's anti-icing system work?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞机的防冰系统如何工作？
cards.referenceText: An anti-icing system operates before or during exposure to prevent ice from forming or adhering on protected areas. Depending on the aircraft, it may use heated air, electric heating or an approved fluid. It protects only the specified surfaces and must be used within the aircraft's procedures and limitations.
cards.referenceTextZh: 防冰系统在进入结冰条件之前或期间工作，以防止冰在受保护区域形成或附着。根据机型不同，它可能使用热空气、电加热或经批准的防冰液。它只能保护指定表面，并且必须在飞机规定的程序和限制内使用。

cards.audioText: What types of airframe ice can form in flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中可能形成哪些类型的机体积冰？
cards.referenceText: The common descriptive types are rime ice, clear ice and mixed ice. Rime ice is usually rough and opaque, while clear ice is smoother and may spread beyond the initial impact area. Mixed ice contains characteristics of both, but pilots may not be able to identify the type reliably in flight.
cards.referenceTextZh: 常见的描述性结冰类型包括雾凇、明冰和混合冰。雾凇通常粗糙且不透明，明冰则较平滑，并可能扩展到最初撞击区域之外。混合冰兼具二者特征，但飞行员在飞行中未必能够可靠判断具体类型。

cards.audioText: Which type of airframe ice poses the greatest threat to flight safety, and why?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪种类型的机体积冰对飞行安全威胁最大？为什么？
cards.referenceText: No single ice type is always the most dangerous because severity depends on accumulation, location and aircraft tolerance. Clear or mixed ice can be especially threatening when it spreads beyond protected surfaces and is difficult to see or remove. Any ice that degrades performance or exceeds the protection system's capability requires immediate attention and exit from the conditions.
cards.referenceTextZh: 没有哪一种冰在所有情况下都一定最危险，因为严重程度取决于积聚量、位置和飞机承受能力。当明冰或混合冰扩展到受保护表面之外，并且难以发现或清除时，尤其危险。任何降低性能或超出防护系统能力的结冰，都需要立即处置并离开相关条件。

cards.audioText: What is the difference between de-icing and anti-icing?
cards.audioTextZh: 除冰与防冰有什么区别？
cards.referenceText: Deicing removes ice, frost or snow that has already formed on a surface. Anti-icing prevents or delays new contamination from forming or adhering. Some systems or ground treatments can support both functions, but crews must understand which function is being used and follow the approved sequence.
cards.referenceTextZh: 除冰是清除已经形成在表面上的冰、霜或雪。防冰则是防止或延缓新的污染物形成或附着。某些系统或地面处理可以兼具两种作用，但机组必须了解当前使用的是哪种功能，并遵循经批准的操作顺序。

cards.audioText: What is holdover time in ground de-icing and anti-icing operations?
cards.audioTextZh: 在地面除冰和防冰作业中，什么是保持时间？
cards.referenceText: Holdover time is the estimated period during which an applied anti-icing fluid is expected to protect treated surfaces from frozen contamination. For a one-step treatment it starts when the treatment begins; for a two-step treatment it starts when the final anti-icing fluid application begins. It is selected from approved current guidance for the actual conditions and is a planning estimate, not a guarantee.
cards.referenceTextZh: 防冰保持时间是指已施用的防冰液预计能够保护处理表面免受冰冻污染物影响的时间。一步法处理从开始施液时计算；两步法处理则从最后一次施用防冰液开始计算。保持时间应根据实际条件，从经批准的现行资料中选取；它只是规划估计，并非保证。

cards.audioText: Why must an aircraft take off within the applicable holdover time after ground de-icing or anti-icing?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞机在地面除冰或防冰后，为什么必须在适用的保持时间内起飞？
cards.referenceText: After the applicable holdover time, the anti-icing fluid may no longer provide the expected protection. Frozen contamination can then form and change the aircraft's aerodynamics. If protection is no longer assured, the crew must follow the approved procedure, which may require a check, retreatment or delaying the takeoff.
cards.referenceTextZh: 超过适用的防冰保持时间后，防冰液可能无法继续提供预期保护。随后可能形成冰冻污染物，并改变飞机的空气动力性能。如果无法确认保护仍然有效，机组必须执行经批准的程序，其中可能包括检查、重新进行除防冰处理或推迟起飞。

cards.audioText: What are the common types of aircraft de-icing and anti-icing fluids?
cards.audioTextZh: 常见的飞机除冰液和防冰液有哪些类型？
cards.referenceText: The common ground deicing and anti-icing fluids are identified as SAE Types I, II, III and IV. Type I is commonly used for removing contamination and provides relatively limited holdover protection. The thicker Types II, III and IV are intended to provide longer anti-icing protection for aircraft and operations for which they are approved.
cards.referenceTextZh: 常见的地面除冰和防冰液分为 SAE I、II、III 和 IV 型。I 型液通常用于清除污染物，提供的保持时间相对较短。较稠的 II、III 和 IV 型液用于为经批准的飞机和运行提供更长时间的防冰保护。

cards.audioText: How do the common types of aircraft de-icing and anti-icing fluids differ?
cards.audioTextZh: 常见类型的飞机除冰液和防冰液有何区别？
cards.referenceText: Type I fluid is relatively thin and is often heated for effective deicing, but it normally offers shorter protection. Types II and IV are thicker anti-icing fluids with longer expected holdover performance, while Type III is formulated for aircraft with lower rotation speeds than those normally suited to Types II and IV. Their use also differs by concentration, temperature, precipitation and aircraft compatibility.
cards.referenceTextZh: I 型液较稀，通常加热后用于有效除冰，但一般只能提供较短保护。II 型和 IV 型是较稠的防冰液，预期保持时间更长；III 型则为较低抬轮速度的飞机配制，这类飞机的抬轮速度低于通常适用 II 型和 IV 型液飞机的抬轮速度。它们的使用还会因浓度、温度、降水和飞机兼容性而不同。

cards.audioText: Who is responsible for deciding whether de-icing or anti-icing is needed before takeoff?
cards.audioTextZh: 起飞前由谁负责决定是否需要除冰或防冰？
cards.referenceText: The pilot in command must be satisfied that the aircraft is safe and meets the clean-aircraft requirements before takeoff. Dispatch, ground personnel and trained deicing staff may provide weather, inspection and treatment information under the operator's program. Their shared duties do not remove the flight crew's responsibility to make the final operational decision.
cards.referenceTextZh: 起飞前，机长必须确认飞机安全，并符合清洁飞机要求。签派人员、地面人员和受训的除冰人员可以按照公司方案提供天气、检查和处理信息。各方共同承担职责，但不能取代飞行机组作出最终运行决定的责任。

cards.audioText: How should the appropriate de-icing or anti-icing fluid be selected in heavy snow?
cards.audioTextZh: 大雪条件下应如何选择合适的除冰液或防冰液？
cards.referenceText: Standard holdover-time tables do not provide a normal holdover time for heavy snow. A crew may operate only under an approved program that gives a valid method for the condition, such as an authorized holdover-time determination system or the required contamination checks. The fluid, mixture and checking method must come from that program and current guidance; otherwise the crew should wait or arrange another approved treatment.
cards.referenceTextZh: 标准保持时间表不会为大雪条件提供常规保持时间。只有在经批准的方案提供了适用于该条件的有效方法时，例如获准使用保持时间判定系统或执行规定的污染检查，机组才可以运行。防冰液、混合比例和检查方法必须来自该方案和现行指导；否则机组应等待或安排其他经批准的处理。

cards.audioText: What is wind shear?
cards.audioTextZh: 什么是风切变？
cards.referenceText: Wind shear is a rapid change in wind speed, direction or both over a relatively short distance. It can change an aircraft's airspeed, lift and flight path very quickly. The hazard is greatest when the aircraft is close to the ground and has little height or energy available for recovery.
cards.referenceTextZh: 风切变是指风速、风向或两者在相对较短距离内迅速变化。它能在极短时间内改变飞机的空速、升力和飞行轨迹。当飞机接近地面、可用于改出的高度或能量很少时，危险最大。

cards.audioText: Where is wind shear most likely to occur?
cards.audioTextZh: 风切变最可能在哪里发生？
cards.referenceText: Wind shear is often found near thunderstorms, microbursts, fronts, temperature inversions and strong surface-wind transitions. It can also occur near mountains, terrain and jet streams. Around an airport, pilots should pay particular attention to low-level alerts, gust fronts and rapidly changing winds.
cards.referenceTextZh: 风切变常见于雷暴、微下击暴流、锋面、逆温层和地面风强烈变化的区域。它也可能出现在山区、地形附近和急流区域。在机场周边，飞行员尤其应注意低空风切变警报、阵风锋和迅速变化的风。

cards.audioText: Have you ever received a wind shear warning in flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中收到过风切变警告吗？
cards.referenceText: An adjustable example is that I once received a predictive wind-shear warning during approach. The crew discontinued the approach, followed the approved procedure and returned only after reassessing the weather. This example shows the desired response but is not a claim of real experience.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个可调整的示范答案是，我曾在进近时收到预测式风切变警告。机组中止了进近，执行了经批准的程序，并在重新评估天气后才再次进近。这个例子用于说明合适的处置方式，并非真实经历陈述。

cards.audioText: What are the possible consequences if a pilot ignores a wind shear warning?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果飞行员忽视风切变警告，可能会造成哪些后果？
cards.referenceText: Ignoring a wind-shear warning can lead to a rapid loss of airspeed, lift and flight-path control. Near the ground, the aircraft may be unable to climb or may strike terrain before the crew can recover. It can also expose the aircraft to severe turbulence, structural loads and an unstable approach or departure.
cards.referenceTextZh: 忽视风切变警告可能导致空速和升力迅速下降，并失去对飞行轨迹的控制。在近地面时，飞机可能无法爬升，或者在机组来不及改出前撞上地形。飞机还可能遭遇严重颠簸和较大的结构载荷，进近或离场也会变得不稳定。

cards.audioText: How are pilots warned about wind shear on your aircraft?
cards.audioTextZh: 你所飞的飞机通过什么方式向飞行员发出风切变警告？
cards.referenceText: A suitable aircraft example would use both predictive and reactive wind-shear functions. The crew may receive visual and aural cautions or warnings from the aircraft, while ATC or airport systems may also issue alerts. The exact sensors, messages, coverage and crew response must be learned from the aircraft manual and operator training.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的飞机示例会同时使用预测式和反应式风切变功能。机组可能收到飞机发出的视觉和音响警戒或警告提示，而空管或机场系统也可能发布警报。具体的传感器、信息、覆盖范围和机组处置必须依据飞机手册和运营人训练掌握。

cards.audioText: Why is wind shear a threat to flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 为什么风切变会威胁飞行安全？
cards.referenceText: Wind shear can change the airflow over the aircraft faster than the crew or engines can compensate. It may produce large airspeed, attitude and vertical-path changes, especially during takeoff or landing. At low altitude, there may be too little time and space to recover from the energy loss.
cards.referenceTextZh: 风切变改变飞机周围气流的速度可能快于机组或发动机的补偿能力。它可能造成空速、姿态和垂直航迹大幅变化，尤其是在起飞或着陆阶段。在低高度时，可能没有足够的时间和空间从能量损失中恢复。

cards.audioText: Have you ever encountered wind shear in flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中遇到过风切变吗？
cards.referenceText: One possible sample answer is: yes, I have encountered moderate wind shear, but not a severe microburst. The crew monitored the trend, followed ATC instructions and kept a safe distance from the reported area. If a warning had occurred, we would have used the trained escape or avoidance procedure.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个可用的示范答案是：是的，我遇到过中度风切变，但没有遇到过严重微下击暴流。机组监控变化趋势，遵守空管指令，并与报告的危险区域保持安全距离。如果当时出现警告，我们会执行训练过的风切变改出或避让程序。

cards.audioText: What should pilots do if they hear a "GO-AROUND, WINDSHEAR AHEAD" warning during approach?
cards.audioTextZh: 进近过程中听到“复飞，前方风切变”警告时，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: The crew should immediately discontinue the approach and carry out the approved wind-shear avoidance or go-around procedure. They should follow the aircraft's guidance, maintain the required flight path and avoid unnecessary configuration changes while the maneuver is being completed. ATC can be advised when workload permits, but flying the aircraft remains the first priority.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组应立即中止进近，并执行经批准的风切变避让或复飞程序。完成机动期间，应遵循飞机引导，保持所需飞行轨迹，并避免不必要的构型变化。工作负荷允许时可以通知空管，但操纵飞机始终是第一要务。

cards.audioText: What should pilots do if they encounter wind shear during the takeoff roll before V1?
cards.audioTextZh: 在 V1 前的起飞滑跑阶段遇到风切变时，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: Before V1, the crew should apply the operator's approved rejected-takeoff and wind-shear criteria. If those criteria require a rejection, the pilot should begin the approved action promptly and maintain directional control using the performance already calculated for the takeoff. The crew must use trained callouts and aircraft-specific actions rather than make a new stopping-distance judgment during the event.
cards.referenceTextZh: 在 V1 之前，机组应采用运营人批准的中断起飞和风切变判据。如果这些判据要求中断起飞，飞行员应立即开始执行经批准的动作，按起飞前已经计算的性能处置，并保持方向控制。机组必须使用训练过的标准喊话和机型特定动作，而不能在事件发生时重新判断停车距离。

cards.audioText: What would you do if you encountered wind shear and a sudden loss of airspeed as the aircraft approached rotation speed?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞机接近抬前轮速度时，如果遭遇风切变并且空速突然下降，你会如何处置？
cards.referenceText: I would keep the aircraft under control and apply the trained takeoff wind-shear procedure. Any decision to reject must be made before V1 so that the stopping action begins no later than V1; if rejection has not begun by V1, the approved plan is normally to continue the takeoff. If airborne, I would follow the aircraft's escape guidance and avoid untrained configuration changes.
cards.referenceTextZh: 我会保持飞机受控，并执行训练过的起飞风切变程序。任何中断起飞的决定都必须在 V1 前作出，确保最迟在 V1 时开始采取停止措施；如果到 V1 尚未开始中断，通常应按批准的计划继续起飞。飞机离地后，我会遵循飞机的风切变改出引导，并避免未经训练的构型变化。

cards.audioText: How can wind shear cause an aircraft to deviate from the glide slope during approach?
cards.audioTextZh: 进近过程中，风切变如何导致飞机偏离下滑道？
cards.referenceText: Wind shear can suddenly change headwind or tailwind components and therefore change lift and vertical speed. The aircraft may rise above or sink below the intended glide path even though the previous approach was stable. Large control and thrust corrections may then be required, making a go-around the safer response if stability criteria are no longer met.
cards.referenceTextZh: 风切变会突然改变顶风或顺风分量，从而改变升力和垂直速度。即使此前进近稳定，飞机也可能升到预定下滑道上方或下沉到其下方。随后可能需要大幅修正操纵和推力；如果不再符合稳定进近标准，复飞会更安全。

cards.audioText: Why is low-level wind shear more hazardous than wind shear at higher altitudes?
cards.audioTextZh: 为什么低空风切变比高空风切变更危险？
cards.referenceText: Low-level wind shear is especially hazardous because the aircraft is slow, configured for takeoff or landing and close to the ground. There is little altitude available to regain energy or correct a sudden flight-path change. Obstacles, runway alignment and high workload further reduce the crew's options.
cards.referenceTextZh: 低空风切变格外危险，因为飞机速度低、处于起飞或着陆构型，并且接近地面。可用于恢复能量或修正突发飞行轨迹变化的高度很少。障碍物、保持跑道方向的要求和较高的工作负荷会进一步减少机组的选择。

cards.audioText: How should pilots respond to a wind shear warning in flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中收到风切变警告时，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: Pilots should take a wind-shear warning seriously and apply the approved avoidance or escape procedure for the phase of flight. They should follow the aircraft guidance, protect the flight path and avoid actions that conflict with the trained maneuver. Once clear and workload permits, they should coordinate with ATC and reassess the plan.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应认真对待风切变警告，并根据所处飞行阶段执行经批准的避让或改出程序。他们应遵循飞机引导、保持对飞行轨迹的控制，并避免采取与训练机动相冲突的动作。脱离危险且工作负荷允许后，应与空管协调并重新评估后续计划。

cards.audioText: What should pilots do if they encounter wind shear during takeoff?
cards.audioTextZh: 起飞过程中遇到风切变时，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: During takeoff, the crew must use the aircraft-specific wind-shear and rejected-takeoff criteria for the actual stage of the takeoff. If the approved decision is to continue or the aircraft is airborne, the pilots should follow the trained escape guidance and prioritize flight-path control. Configuration, automation and ATC communication should be managed exactly as trained, not by a generic fixed sequence.
cards.referenceTextZh: 起飞时，机组必须根据实际起飞阶段采用机型特定的风切变和中断起飞判据。如果按批准判据应继续起飞，或者飞机已经离地，飞行员应遵循训练过的风切变改出引导，并优先控制飞行轨迹。构型、自动化和空管通信都应按训练要求管理，而不是套用通用的固定顺序。

cards.audioText: How can wind shear affect aircraft performance?
cards.audioTextZh: 风切变会如何影响飞机性能？
cards.referenceText: Wind shear can cause rapid changes in indicated airspeed, lift, vertical speed and required thrust. A downdraft or increasing tailwind can reduce climb performance, while an initial headwind gain may be followed by a severe loss. These changes can overwhelm the available performance when the aircraft is close to the ground.
cards.referenceTextZh: 风切变会使指示空速、升力、垂直速度和所需推力迅速变化。下沉气流或增强的顺风会降低爬升性能，而最初获得的顶风增益之后可能出现严重的空速和性能损失。当飞机接近地面时，这些变化可能超过飞机可用性能。

cards.audioText: What would you do if low-level wind shear were forecast for takeoff?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果预报起飞时会出现低空风切变，你会如何处置？
cards.referenceText: I would review the forecast, airport alerts, runway options and company wind-shear guidance before departure. If the risk were significant, I would delay the takeoff, select a safer runway or wait for the cell or gust front to move away. A performance margin or warning system does not justify departing into a known hazardous microburst.
cards.referenceTextZh: 起飞前，我会检查预报、机场警报、跑道选择和公司的风切变指南。如果风险较高，我会推迟起飞、选择更安全的跑道，或者等待雷暴单体或阵风锋移开。性能裕度或警告系统并不能成为飞入已知危险微下击暴流的理由。

cards.audioText: How can pilots recognize that they have encountered wind shear?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行员如何判断飞机已经遭遇风切变？
cards.referenceText: The crew may notice unexpected changes in airspeed, vertical speed, pitch, thrust demand or flight-path deviation. Onboard systems may issue a reactive warning, and the aircraft may encounter strong downdrafts or turbulence. Pilots should respond to the total indications and trained alerts rather than wait to prove the exact weather phenomenon.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组可能会发现空速、垂直速度、俯仰、推力需求或飞行轨迹出现意外变化。机载系统可能发出反应式警告，飞机也可能遭遇强烈下沉气流或颠簸。飞行员应综合各种指示，并按训练中规定的警报处置，而不是等待确认具体是哪一种天气现象。

cards.audioText: What measures can help reduce accidents caused by wind shear?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪些措施有助于减少风切变造成的事故？
cards.referenceText: Accidents can be reduced through reliable forecasting and airport detection, timely ATC alerts and disciplined avoidance decisions. Aircraft warning systems, simulator training and clear escape procedures help crews recognize and respond to the hazard. Operators should also use reports and data to improve training without encouraging penetration of dangerous weather.
cards.referenceTextZh: 可靠的预报和机场探测、及时的空管警报以及严格执行避让决策，都能减少事故。飞机警告系统、模拟机训练和明确的风切变改出程序有助于机组识别并应对危险。运营人还应利用报告和数据改进训练，但不能因此鼓励机组穿越危险天气。

cards.audioText: During which seasons is wind shear most likely to occur?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪些季节最容易出现风切变？
cards.referenceText: There is no single wind-shear season everywhere. Convective wind shear and microbursts are often more common in warm seasons when thunderstorms are frequent, while frontal and mountain-related shear can occur in other seasons. Pilots should use local climatology and current weather rather than rely only on the calendar.
cards.referenceTextZh: 世界各地并不存在统一的风切变季节。由对流引起的风切变和微下击暴流通常在雷暴频繁的暖季更常见，而锋面或山区相关的风切变也可能出现在其他季节。飞行员应依据当地气候特点和当前天气，而不能只看日历。

cards.audioText: What is runway visual range (RVR)?
cards.audioTextZh: 什么是跑道视程（RVR）？
cards.referenceText: Runway visual range is the distance over which a pilot on the runway centerline can see the runway markings or the lights that define the runway or its centerline. It is normally assessed by instruments and may be reported for touchdown, midpoint and rollout positions. RVR is used with the applicable takeoff or landing requirements in low visibility.
cards.referenceTextZh: 跑道视程是指位于跑道中线上的飞行员能够看清跑道标志，或者看清用于界定跑道或跑道中线的灯光时所对应的距离。它通常由仪器测量，并可能分别报告接地区、中点和滑跑端的数值。在低能见度条件下，RVR 与适用的起飞或着陆要求结合使用。

cards.audioText: When should pilots obtain current RVR information?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行员应在什么时候获取最新的 RVR 信息？
cards.referenceText: Pilots should obtain current RVR when it is relevant to departure, approach or landing minima. They should check it before making the operational decision and monitor updates when visibility is changing. The applicable regulation, published procedure, operating minima and operator authorization determine which reported value must be used.
cards.referenceTextZh: 当 RVR 与离场、进近或着陆最低标准有关时，飞行员应获取现行数值。机组应在作出运行决定前核对 RVR，并在能见度变化时持续关注更新。适用法规、公布程序、运行最低标准和运营人批准，共同决定必须使用哪一个报告值。

cards.audioText: From what sources can pilots obtain RVR information?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行员可以从哪些来源获取 RVR 信息？
cards.referenceText: Pilots normally receive official RVR through ATIS or directly from ATC when the airport system is operating. It may also appear in approved operational weather or data-link services used for planning. The crew should confirm that the value is current and official for the runway and operation concerned.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机场 RVR 系统工作时，飞行员通常通过 ATIS 或直接从 ATC 获得官方数值。规划时采用的经批准的航空运行气象服务，或经批准的数据链服务中也可能显示 RVR。机组应确认该数值对相关跑道和运行而言是现行且官方的数据。

cards.audioText: When are low-visibility procedures required?
cards.audioTextZh: 何时需要实施低能见度程序？
cards.referenceText: Low-visibility procedures are required when the reported conditions fall below the trigger established for that airport and operation. They protect runway and taxiway movements and may preserve sensitive areas for instrument approaches. The crew should follow the published airport procedures, ATC instructions and its operator's approved limits rather than assume one universal RVR value.
cards.referenceTextZh: 当报告条件低于该机场和运行规定的启动标准时，就需要实施低能见度程序。这些程序用于保护跑道和滑行道活动，并可能保护仪表进近的敏感区。机组应遵守机场公布程序、ATC 指令和本公司经批准的限制，而不能假定存在一个通用的 RVR 数值。

cards.audioText: What is your company's policy on takeoffs in low-visibility conditions?
cards.audioTextZh: 贵公司对低能见度条件下起飞有什么规定？
cards.referenceText: A suitable company example would be that low-visibility takeoff is permitted only when the airport, aircraft, crew and operator are approved for it and the reported values meet the applicable minima. The crew must complete the required briefing, verify relevant systems and follow the low-visibility taxi and takeoff procedures. If any required condition is not met, the takeoff is delayed or cancelled.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的公司示范答案是：只有机场、飞机、机组和运营人都具备相应批准，并且报告值满足适用最低标准时，才允许低能见度起飞。机组必须完成规定简令，确认相关系统，并遵循低能见度滑行和起飞程序。如果任何必要条件不满足，就应推迟或取消起飞。

cards.audioText: What is your company's policy on landings in low-visibility conditions?
cards.audioTextZh: 贵公司对低能见度条件下着陆有什么规定？
cards.referenceText: One model company policy would allow a low-visibility landing only when the approach, runway facilities, aircraft, crew and operator have the necessary approval and all applicable minima are met. The crew would review system status, approach requirements and missed-approach considerations before continuing. If the required visual reference or another limiting condition is not satisfied, the crew would go around and use the approved alternative plan.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个公司政策示范答案是：只有进近程序、跑道设施、飞机、机组和运营人都具备必要批准，并且满足所有适用最低标准时，才允许低能见度着陆。继续进近前，机组应检查系统状态、进近要求和复飞考虑事项。如果不能获得所需目视参考，或其他限制条件不满足，机组应复飞并执行经批准的备选方案。

cards.audioText: How can pilots prevent runway incursions while taxiing in low visibility?
cards.audioTextZh: 低能见度滑行时，飞行员如何防止跑道侵入？
cards.referenceText: Pilots should use the airport chart, follow the assigned route and maintain a sterile, well-monitored taxi operation. Both pilots should confirm clearances, signs, markings and position, and stop when there is doubt. A runway must not be entered or crossed without a clear authorization and positive identification.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应使用机场图，按照指定路线滑行，保持无干扰驾驶舱纪律，并严密监控滑行。两名飞行员都应确认许可、标志、标线和飞机位置，存在疑问时立即停止。没有明确许可和确切识别，不得进入或穿越跑道。

cards.audioText: What precautions should pilots take when taxiing in low visibility?
cards.audioTextZh: 低能见度滑行时，飞行员应采取哪些预防措施？
cards.referenceText: The crew should taxi at a controllable speed, use the airport moving map if approved and keep the chart and cleared route under continuous review. Exterior lights, stop bars and other visual aids should be used as required, but never as a substitute for clearance. If position or instruction becomes uncertain, the aircraft should stop and ask ATC for clarification.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组应以可控速度滑行；如果获准使用机场移动地图，应将其与机场图和管制许可路线持续对照。外部灯光、停止排灯和其他目视辅助设施应按要求使用，但绝不能代替管制许可。如果对位置或指令不确定，飞机应停止并请求 ATC 澄清。

cards.audioText: How can pilots prevent ground collisions in low-visibility conditions?
cards.audioTextZh: 低能见度条件下，飞行员如何防止地面碰撞？
cards.referenceText: Ground-collision risk can be reduced by accurate position awareness, strict clearance readback and disciplined taxi monitoring. The crew should control speed, scan for aircraft, vehicles and obstacles, and use all approved surface guidance. When the route is unclear or another object cannot be positively assessed, stopping is safer than continuing.
cards.referenceTextZh: 准确掌握位置、严格复诵许可并进行规范、严密的滑行监控，可以降低地面相撞风险。机组应控制速度，观察飞机、车辆和障碍物，并使用所有经批准的场面引导手段。当路线不清楚或无法确切判断其他物体时，停车比继续滑行更安全。

cards.audioText: What should a pilot do after missing the correct taxiway in low visibility?
cards.audioTextZh: 低能见度下错过正确滑行道后，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: The pilot should not turn unpredictably or try to recover the route without clearance. The aircraft should stop in a safe position, advise ATC that the taxiway was missed and request amended instructions. The crew should then verify the new route on the chart before moving again.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员不应突然转弯，也不应在没有许可的情况下自行找回路线。飞机应停在安全位置，通知 ATC 已错过滑行道，并请求新的指令。再次移动前，机组应在机场图上确认新路线。

cards.audioText: What consequences can result from disorientation in low-visibility conditions?
cards.audioTextZh: 低能见度条件下迷失方向可能导致哪些后果？
cards.referenceText: Disorientation can lead to a taxiway deviation, runway incursion, collision or entry into an unsafe area. It also raises workload and can cause the crew to misunderstand later instructions. Recognizing uncertainty early, stopping and obtaining help prevents a small navigation error from becoming an accident.
cards.referenceTextZh: 迷失方向可能导致偏离滑行道、跑道侵入、碰撞或进入不安全区域。它还会增加工作负荷，并可能使机组误解后续指令。及早意识到自己不能确定位置或指令、停车并寻求帮助，可以防止小的导航错误演变成事故。

cards.audioText: What hazards can arise during low-visibility operations?
cards.audioTextZh: 低能见度运行中可能出现哪些危险？
cards.referenceText: Low visibility reduces the crew's ability to see traffic, markings, obstacles and the runway environment. It increases the risk of runway incursions, ground collisions, navigation errors and loss of situational awareness. It can also limit takeoff and landing options, so careful planning, strict procedures and conservative decisions are essential.
cards.referenceTextZh: 低能见度会降低机组观察交通、标线、障碍物和跑道环境的能力。它会增加跑道侵入、地面碰撞、导航错误和态势感知丧失的风险。它还可能限制起飞和着陆选择，因此周密规划、严格执行程序和保守决策至关重要。

cards.audioText: Have you ever encountered turbulence during a flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中遇到过颠簸吗？
cards.referenceText: A model personal answer is that I have experienced light to moderate turbulence on several flights. The crew turned on the seat-belt sign, adjusted the operation as required and asked ATC about smoother conditions. The event was manageable because it was anticipated and the cabin was secured.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个个人示范答案是，我在几次飞行中遇到过轻度至中度颠簸。机组打开安全带指示灯，采取所需的运行调整，并向空管询问更平稳的飞行条件。由于事先有所预期，且客舱内人员、设备和物品已经固定妥当，整个事件处于可控范围。

cards.audioText: Do you think turbulence is dangerous to flight safety? Why or why not?
cards.audioTextZh: 你认为颠簸会危及飞行安全吗？为什么？
cards.referenceText: Turbulence can be dangerous, especially when it is severe or unexpected. Unrestrained occupants may be injured, and the aircraft can experience large airspeed, altitude or attitude changes. Most routine turbulence is managed safely, but crews must respect forecasts, reports and aircraft limitations.
cards.referenceTextZh: 颠簸可能很危险，严重或突发的颠簸尤其如此。未系安全带的人员可能受伤，飞机的空速、高度或姿态也可能大幅变化。大多数常见颠簸都能得到安全处置，但机组必须重视预报、报告和飞机限制。

cards.audioText: Why is severe turbulence dangerous?
cards.audioTextZh: 为什么严重颠簸很危险？
cards.referenceText: Severe turbulence can cause abrupt and large changes in altitude, attitude and airspeed, and the aircraft may be momentarily difficult to control. It can injure occupants and impose high loads on the structure. It also increases the risk of altitude deviation and traffic conflict in reduced-separation airspace.
cards.referenceTextZh: 严重颠簸可能使高度、姿态和空速突然大幅变化，飞机也可能暂时难以控制。它可能造成人员受伤，并使机体承受较大载荷。在缩小垂直间隔空域内，它还会增加高度偏差和飞行冲突的风险。

cards.audioText: What damage can severe turbulence cause?
cards.audioTextZh: 严重颠簸会造成哪些损伤？
cards.referenceText: Severe turbulence can damage cabin fittings and unsecured equipment, and it may cause serious injuries. In the formal reporting scale, structural damage is associated more clearly with extreme turbulence, although any suspected exceedance still requires assessment. The crew should report the encounter and arrange the inspections required by the aircraft and operator procedures.
cards.referenceTextZh: 严重颠簸可能损坏客舱设施和未固定的设备，也可能造成重伤。在正式报告等级中，结构损伤与极度颠簸的对应关系更明确，但只要怀疑出现超限，仍需进行评估。机组应报告这次遭遇，并按飞机和运营人程序安排所需检查。

cards.audioText: What procedures should pilots follow to avoid clear-air turbulence?
cards.audioTextZh: 为避免晴空颠簸，飞行员应遵循哪些程序？
cards.referenceText: Pilots should review significant weather information, turbulence forecasts, jet-stream and mountain-wave conditions, and recent pilot or automated reports. In flight, they should monitor updates and request a route or altitude with lower reported risk when practical. CAT cannot always be seen or completely avoided, so the cabin should be secured before a likely encounter.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应查看重要天气资料、颠簸预报、急流和山地波状况，以及近期的飞行员报告或自动化报告。飞行中应持续关注更新，并在可行时申请风险报告较低的航路或高度。晴空颠簸并不总是可见，也无法完全避开，因此应在可能遭遇前确保客舱内人员、设备和物品固定妥当。

cards.audioText: What threats does clear-air turbulence pose to flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 晴空颠簸会对飞行安全构成哪些威胁？
cards.referenceText: Clear-air turbulence may occur without visible clouds, so it can surprise both crew and passengers. It can cause injuries, altitude or airspeed deviations and high structural loads. Its association with jet streams and wind shear also means that nearby smooth air can change quickly.
cards.referenceTextZh: 晴空颠簸可能出现在没有可见云层的区域，因此机组和旅客都可能猝不及防。它可能造成人员受伤、高度或空速偏差以及较大的结构载荷。它与急流和风切变相关，也意味着附近的平稳空气可能迅速发生变化。

cards.audioText: How can pilots reduce the risks of turbulence during flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中，飞行员如何降低颠簸带来的风险？
cards.referenceText: Pilots can reduce risk by planning with current forecasts and reports, keeping the cabin and crew secured, and warning the cabin early. If turbulence is encountered, they should use the recommended speed and procedure for the aircraft and coordinate route or altitude changes with ATC. Significant turbulence should be reported so other crews can make better decisions.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员可以通过使用最新预报和报告进行计划、确保机组与客舱内人员、设备和物品安全，并提前通知客舱机组来降低风险。遇到颠簸时，应采用该机型建议的速度和程序，并与空管协调改变航路或高度。应报告对运行有显著影响的颠簸，以便其他机组作出更好的决定。

cards.audioText: What is clear-air turbulence (CAT)?
cards.audioTextZh: 什么是晴空颠簸（CAT）？
cards.referenceText: Clear-air turbulence is turbulence encountered where no clouds are present. The term is commonly used for high-level turbulence associated with wind shear, often near a jet stream. Because it may lack a visible warning, forecasts and reports are important for managing the risk.
cards.referenceTextZh: 晴空颠簸是指在无云区域遇到的颠簸。这个术语通常用于描述与风切变有关、常出现在急流附近的高空颠簸。由于它可能没有可见预兆，预报和报告对于风险管理十分重要。

cards.audioText: How can mountain-wave turbulence affect flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 山岳波颠簸会如何影响飞行安全？
cards.referenceText: Mountain waves can cause strong updrafts and downdrafts, airspeed fluctuations and altitude deviations, sometimes with severe turbulence. They may make altitude keeping difficult and create traffic risk in reduced-separation airspace. The effect can be localized and may occur with little obvious cloud, so forecasts, reports and conservative routing are important.
cards.referenceTextZh: 山地波可能产生强烈上升和下沉气流、空速波动及高度偏差，有时还伴有严重颠簸。它会使保持高度变得困难，并在缩小垂直间隔空域内造成飞行冲突风险。其影响可能局部出现，也可能没有明显云层，因此预报、报告和保守选择航路很重要。

cards.audioText: How can pilots detect cumulonimbus clouds or thunderstorms ahead during flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中，飞行员如何探测前方的积雨云或雷暴？
cards.referenceText: Pilots can detect cumulonimbus clouds visually when conditions permit and by using airborne weather radar correctly. Lightning information, satellite or data-link weather, ATC alerts and pilot reports provide additional evidence. No single source is complete, so the crew should compare the information and avoid suspicious convective areas.
cards.referenceTextZh: 条件允许时，飞行员可以通过目视观察和正确使用机载气象雷达来探测积雨云。雷电信息、卫星或数据链天气资料、空管警报和飞行员报告可以提供补充依据。任何单一信息源都不完整，因此机组应相互对照，并避开可疑的对流区域。

cards.audioText: What hazards can cumulonimbus clouds and thunderstorms pose to an aircraft?
cards.audioTextZh: 积雨云和雷暴会给飞机带来哪些危险？
cards.referenceText: Cumulonimbus clouds can contain severe turbulence, wind shear, microbursts, hail, lightning, icing and intense precipitation. Strong updrafts and downdrafts can cause major altitude and airspeed changes or loss of control. Hail and turbulence may also exist outside the visible cloud, so avoiding only the darkest center is not enough.
cards.referenceTextZh: 积雨云内部可能有严重颠簸、风切变、微下击暴流、冰雹、闪电、结冰和强降水。强烈上升和下沉气流可能造成高度与空速大幅变化，甚至导致失控。冰雹和颠簸也可能出现在可见云体之外，因此只避开颜色最深的中心区域并不足够。

cards.audioText: Have you ever encountered a cumulonimbus cloud or thunderstorm during a flight? If so, what happened?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中遇到过积雨云或雷暴吗？如果遇到过，当时发生了什么？
cards.referenceText: One adjustable example is that I once saw a developing thunderstorm near the planned route. The crew used radar and ATC information to deviate early and maintain the separation required by our approved procedure. We did not enter the cloud, and the flight continued normally after the deviation.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个可调整的示范答案是，我曾看到计划航路附近有雷暴正在发展。机组利用雷达和空管信息提前绕飞，并保持经批准程序要求的间隔。我们没有进入云体，绕飞后航班继续正常运行。

cards.audioText: How does a thunderstorm cell appear on the cockpit weather radar display?
cards.audioTextZh: 雷暴单体在驾驶舱气象雷达显示器上呈现什么样子？
cards.referenceText: A thunderstorm usually appears as an area of stronger precipitation returns, with colors or levels changing according to the radar display design. The shape, gradient and movement may help the crew recognize a cell, but color alone does not show every hazard. Tilt, gain if available, range and attenuation must be considered when interpreting the image.
cards.referenceTextZh: 雷暴在雷达上通常表现为较强的降水回波区，颜色或等级会随雷达显示设计而变化。回波的形状、梯度和移动可能有助于机组识别单体，但仅凭颜色无法显示所有危险。解读图像时必须考虑天线俯仰、显示量程和衰减；设备具备增益调节功能时，还应考虑增益设置。

cards.audioText: What should a pilot do if the weather radar indicates a thunderstorm ahead?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果气象雷达显示前方有雷暴，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: The pilot should avoid the thunderstorm and plan a deviation early rather than use the radar to find a path through the cell. The crew should consider cell movement, surrounding cells, the escape route and ATC coordination. If a safe deviation is not available, delaying, holding only in safe weather, diverting or turning back may be necessary.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应避开雷暴并尽早规划绕飞，而不能用雷达寻找穿过单体的通道。机组应考虑单体移动、周边单体、脱离路线和空管协调。如果无法安全绕飞，可能需要推迟起飞、只在安全天气区域等待、备降或返航。

cards.audioText: How does airborne weather radar estimate the intensity of precipitation?
cards.audioTextZh: 机载气象雷达如何估算降水强度？
cards.referenceText: Airborne weather radar transmits energy and measures the energy reflected by precipitation. Stronger returns generally indicate greater reflectivity, which the system converts into display levels or colors. Reflectivity is not a direct measurement of turbulence, hail or updraft strength, so pilots must interpret it with other information.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机载气象雷达发射能量，并测量降水反射回来的能量。回波越强，通常表示反射率越高，系统会将其转换为不同显示等级或颜色。反射率并不直接测量颠簸、冰雹或上升气流强度，因此飞行员必须结合其他信息进行判断。

cards.audioText: What is the main purpose of airborne weather radar?
cards.audioTextZh: 机载气象雷达的主要用途是什么？
cards.referenceText: The main purpose of airborne weather radar is to help the crew detect and avoid hazardous precipitation and associated convective weather ahead. It supports route planning and tactical deviation decisions. It is not designed to guarantee a safe route through a thunderstorm or display every weather hazard.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机载气象雷达的主要用途是帮助机组探测并避开前方危险降水及相关对流天气。它可以辅助航路规划和临时绕飞决策。它不能保证存在一条安全穿越雷暴的航路，也不能显示每一种天气危险。

cards.audioText: How can pilots use airborne weather radar to avoid thunderstorms?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行员如何使用机载气象雷达避开雷暴？
cards.referenceText: Pilots should use the correct range and tilt to build a three-dimensional understanding of the returns and identify developing or hidden cells. They should compare the radar picture with forecasts, lightning, visual cues and reports, then deviate with an approved margin and escape option. Radar should support avoidance, not close-range penetration between strong returns.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应正确选择显示量程和天线俯仰，以形成对回波的三维认识，并识别正在发展或被遮蔽的单体。他们应将雷达图像与预报、雷电、目视线索和报告相互对照，再按批准的间隔绕飞，并预留安全脱离方案。雷达应当用于避让，而不是支持在强回波之间近距离穿越。

cards.audioText: What are the limitations of weather radar?
cards.audioTextZh: 气象雷达有哪些局限性？
cards.referenceText: Weather radar mainly detects precipitation, so it may not show dry turbulence or all non-precipitation hazards. Heavy precipitation can attenuate the signal and hide dangerous weather behind a strong return, while poor tilt or range selection can create a misleading picture. Ground clutter, radome contamination and equipment limits also affect interpretation.
cards.referenceTextZh: 气象雷达主要探测降水，因此可能无法显示干性颠簸或所有非降水危险。强降水会使信号衰减，并遮蔽强回波后方的危险天气；俯仰或显示量程选择不当也可能形成误导性图像。地面杂波、雷达罩污染和设备限制同样会影响判读。

cards.audioText: What conditions are needed for a thunderstorm to develop?
cards.audioTextZh: 雷暴形成需要哪些条件？
cards.referenceText: A thunderstorm needs moisture, unstable air and a lifting mechanism. Lifting may come from surface heating, a front, terrain or another weather boundary. When these ingredients are strong enough, deep convection and a cumulonimbus cloud can develop.
cards.referenceTextZh: 形成雷暴需要水汽、不稳定空气和抬升机制。抬升可能来自地面受热、锋面、地形或其他天气边界。当这些条件足够强时，就可能发展出深厚对流和积雨云。

cards.audioText: What are the stages in the life cycle of a thunderstorm?
cards.audioTextZh: 雷暴的生命周期分为哪些阶段？
cards.referenceText: The usual life-cycle stages are developing, mature and dissipating. The developing stage is dominated by updrafts, while the mature stage contains both strong updrafts and downdrafts and normally presents the greatest range of hazards. In the dissipating stage, downdrafts dominate, but lightning, turbulence and outflow can remain dangerous.
cards.referenceTextZh: 雷暴通常经历发展、成熟和消散三个阶段。发展阶段以上升气流为主，成熟阶段同时存在强烈上升和下沉气流，通常包含种类最多的危险。消散阶段以下沉气流为主，但闪电、颠簸和外流仍可能很危险。

cards.audioText: What should pilots consider when deviating around a thunderstorm?
cards.audioTextZh: 绕飞雷暴时，飞行员应考虑哪些因素？
cards.referenceText: The crew should consider cell movement, growth, wind, nearby cells, the anvil area and the route after the deviation. It should maintain the approved avoidance margin, keep a clear escape path and avoid being trapped between cells. Terrain, fuel, traffic, airspace and ATC clearance also affect the safest plan.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组应考虑单体的移动和发展、风、邻近单体、砧状云区以及绕飞后的航路。应保持批准的避让间隔，始终保留一条畅通可用的脱离路线，并避免被困在多个单体之间。地形、燃油、交通、空域和空管许可也会影响最安全的方案。

cards.audioText: In which season is a thunderstorm most likely to occur?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪个季节最容易出现雷暴？
cards.referenceText: Thunderstorms are often most frequent during warm seasons because heating and moisture support convection. However, frontal thunderstorms can occur in other seasons, and tropical regions may have different patterns. Pilots should use local climatology and current forecasts rather than assume a season is free of thunderstorms.
cards.referenceTextZh: 雷暴通常在暖季最频繁，因为地表受热和水汽有利于对流发展。不过，锋面雷暴也可能出现在其他季节，热带地区还可能有不同规律。飞行员应依据当地气候特点和当前预报，不能假定某个季节没有雷暴。

cards.audioText: What should a pilot do if a thunderstorm is affecting the airport?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果雷暴正在影响机场，飞行员应如何处置？
cards.referenceText: The pilot should assess whether the airport, approach or departure path is affected by the cell, outflow, lightning or wind shear. A safe choice may be to delay, hold only in a safe area, divert or use another suitable airport or runway. The crew should not continue merely because the runway is technically open.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应评估机场、进近或离场航径是否受到单体、外流、闪电或风切变影响。安全选择可能是推迟起飞、只在安全区域等待、备降，或者使用另一个合适的机场或跑道。机组不能仅因为跑道尚未关闭就继续运行。

cards.audioText: What actions should a pilot take when encountering a strong crosswind on approach?
cards.audioTextZh: 进近过程中遇到强侧风时，飞行员应采取哪些措施？
cards.referenceText: The crew should confirm the crosswind, gusts, runway condition and applicable limits, then use the approved crosswind technique and a stabilized approach. It should monitor drift, speed and control margin continuously. If the aircraft cannot remain stable or aligned, the pilot should go around and select a safer option.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组应确认侧风、阵风、跑道状况和适用限制，然后采用批准的侧风技术并保持稳定进近。应持续监控偏流、速度和操纵裕度。如果飞机无法保持稳定或对准跑道，飞行员应复飞并选择更安全的方案。

cards.audioText: How would you respond if the preceding aircraft went around because of strong crosswinds?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果前机因强侧风复飞，你会如何处置？
cards.referenceText: I would treat the preceding go-around as important new information and reassess the wind and runway conditions. I would ask for details if available, maintain spacing and prepare to go around rather than assume my aircraft would succeed. If the conditions were near or beyond my limits, I would delay or use another runway or airport.
cards.referenceTextZh: 我会把前机复飞视为重要的新信息，并重新评估风和跑道状况。如果能够获得细节，我会主动询问，保持间隔并做好复飞准备，而不会认为自己的飞机一定能够成功着陆。如果条件接近或超过我的限制，我会等待或改用其他跑道或机场。

cards.audioText: Do you consider a crosswind landing particularly hazardous? Why or why not?
cards.audioTextZh: 你认为侧风着陆特别危险吗？为什么？
cards.referenceText: A crosswind landing is not automatically hazardous when it is within limits and the crew is trained and current. The risk increases with gusts, contamination, poor visibility or limited control margin. A stable approach and willingness to go around are more important than proving that the landing can be completed.
cards.referenceTextZh: 只要处于限制范围内，而且机组受过训练并保持近期经历，侧风着陆并非一定危险。阵风、跑道污染、能见度不佳或操纵裕度有限都会增加风险。保持稳定进近并愿意复飞，比证明一定能完成着陆更重要。

cards.audioText: How would you decide whether to continue an approach when the crosswind is close to the applicable limit?
cards.audioTextZh: 当侧风接近适用限制时，你会如何决定是否继续进近？
cards.referenceText: I would compare the current and gusting crosswind with the most restrictive applicable aircraft, runway, company and crew limit. I would also consider runway condition, wind variability, approach stability, recent reports and the available alternate plan. When the margin is small or the trend is worsening, a go-around or diversion is the safer decision.
cards.referenceTextZh: 我会将当前侧风值及阵风条件下的侧风值与适用的飞机、跑道、公司和机组限制进行比较，并采用其中最严格的一项。我还会考虑跑道状况、风的变化、进近稳定性、近期报告和可用备选方案。当裕度很小或趋势正在恶化时，复飞或备降更安全。

cards.audioText: What preparations should pilots make before arriving at a destination where strong crosswinds are forecast?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果预报目的地有强侧风，飞行员在到达前应做哪些准备？
cards.referenceText: Pilots should review forecast and observed winds, gusts, runway options, runway condition and all applicable limits before arrival. They should calculate landing performance, brief the crosswind technique and go-around plan, and identify a suitable alternate. Updated ATIS, ATC reports and reports from other aircraft should be monitored because conditions may change quickly.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员在到达前应查看预报风和实测风、阵风、跑道选择、跑道状况及所有适用限制。应计算着陆性能，在简令中说明侧风技术和复飞计划，并确定合适的备降场。由于条件可能迅速变化，还应持续关注最新 ATIS、空管报告和其他飞机的报告。

cards.audioText: What would you do if the crosswind exceeded the applicable limit but the other pilot insisted on landing?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果侧风超过适用限制，但另一名飞行员坚持着陆，你会如何处理？
cards.referenceText: I would state clearly that landing beyond an applicable limit is not acceptable and call for a go-around. I would use calm, assertive CRM and refer to the approved limit and safer alternatives. If disagreement remained, I would continue to protect the aircraft and report the safety concern through the proper process after landing.
cards.referenceTextZh: 我会明确指出，超出适用限制着陆不可接受，并要求复飞。我会采用冷静而坚定的机组资源管理沟通，说明批准的限制和更安全的替代方案。如果分歧仍然存在，我会继续保护飞机安全，并在着陆后通过适当程序报告安全问题。

cards.audioText: What should a flight crew monitor closely during a crosswind landing?
cards.audioTextZh: 侧风着陆过程中，机组应密切监控哪些事项？
cards.referenceText: The crew should monitor approach stability, airspeed and gust response, drift, runway alignment and the remaining control margin. During touchdown and rollout, it should watch the touchdown point, centerline, bank angle, drift and directional control. Any unstable trend or unacceptable touchdown geometry should lead to the approved go-around decision while that option remains available.
cards.referenceTextZh: 机组应监控进近稳定性、空速和阵风响应、偏流、跑道对正情况及剩余操纵裕度。接地和滑跑期间，应关注接地点、中线、坡度、偏移和方向控制。只要仍可复飞，任何不稳定趋势，或接地点、对正和姿态等几何关系不可接受，都应触发经批准的复飞决定。

cards.audioText: What can happen if an aircraft lands in a strong crosswind?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞机在强侧风中着陆可能会发生什么？
cards.referenceText: A poorly controlled strong-crosswind landing can cause runway excursion, hard landing, wingtip or engine contact, tire or landing-gear damage and excessive side loads. Gusts can also produce a long or unstable touchdown. Correct technique, limits and a timely go-around reduce these risks.
cards.referenceTextZh: 强侧风着陆控制不当可能造成冲出跑道、重着陆、翼尖或发动机擦地、轮胎或起落架损坏以及过大的侧向载荷。阵风还可能造成接地点过远或接地不稳定。正确技术、遵守限制和及时复飞可以降低这些风险。

cards.audioText: What is a microburst?
cards.audioTextZh: 什么是微下击暴流？
cards.referenceText: A microburst is a small but intense downdraft that reaches the ground and spreads outward. An aircraft crossing it may first experience increasing headwind, then a downdraft and finally a strong tailwind. This rapid sequence can produce a severe loss of performance close to the ground.
cards.referenceTextZh: 微下击暴流是一股范围较小但强度很大的下沉气流，到达地面后会向外扩散。飞机穿越时可能先遇到增强的顶风，随后是下沉气流，最后是强顺风。这一快速变化过程会使飞机在近地面时严重损失性能。

cards.audioText: How can a microburst threaten flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 微下击暴流会如何威胁飞行安全？
cards.referenceText: A microburst can change airspeed and lift faster than the aircraft can regain energy. Its downdraft and outflow may prevent a safe climb or cause a rapid descent during approach. Because it is concentrated near the ground, recovery time and altitude are very limited.
cards.referenceTextZh: 微下击暴流改变空速和升力的速度可能快于飞机重新获得能量的速度。其下沉气流和外流可能使飞机无法安全爬升，或在进近时迅速下降。由于它集中出现在近地面区域，可用于改出的时间和高度十分有限。

cards.audioText: Under what weather conditions are microbursts most likely to occur?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪些天气条件下最容易出现微下击暴流？
cards.referenceText: Microbursts are commonly associated with convective clouds, thunderstorms and strong precipitation shafts. They can also form when precipitation evaporates into dry air below a cloud, producing a strong cooled downdraft. Pilots should consider airport alerts and the whole convective environment, not only whether heavy rain is reaching the ground.
cards.referenceTextZh: 微下击暴流通常与对流云、雷暴和强降水柱有关。当降水在云下干燥空气中蒸发并形成强烈冷却下沉气流时，它也可能产生。飞行员应综合考虑机场警报和整个对流环境，不能只看大雨是否已经到达地面。

cards.audioText: What could happen if an aircraft flew through a microburst?
cards.audioTextZh: 如果飞机穿越微下击暴流，可能会发生什么？
cards.referenceText: The aircraft could experience a rapid airspeed gain followed by a severe loss, strong downdraft and large flight-path deviation. During takeoff or approach, it might be unable to climb or maintain clearance from the ground. An unrecognized or mishandled encounter can therefore result in loss of control or impact with terrain.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞机可能先出现空速迅速增加，随后严重下降，并遭遇强烈下沉气流和大幅飞行轨迹偏差。在起飞或进近期间，它可能无法爬升或保持离地间隔。因此，如果未能识别微下击暴流或处置不当，就可能导致失控或撞地。

cards.audioText: What factors would you consider if you encountered heavy rain during approach?
cards.audioTextZh: 进近过程中遇到大雨时，你会考虑哪些因素？
cards.referenceText: I would consider visibility, runway condition and braking action, crosswind, wind shear and thunderstorm activity, and the approach's stability. I would also check aircraft limitations, landing performance and the risk of engine or sensor effects from intense precipitation. If the approach could not remain stable or the runway margin were doubtful, I would go around or use another plan.
cards.referenceTextZh: 我会考虑能见度、跑道状况和制动效应、侧风、风切变、雷暴活动以及进近稳定性。我还会检查飞机限制、着陆性能，以及强降水对发动机或传感器的潜在影响。如果进近无法保持稳定，或跑道裕度存在疑问，我会复飞或采用其他方案。

cards.audioText: Have you ever flown in heavy rain?
cards.audioTextZh: 你曾在大雨中飞行过吗？
cards.referenceText: One adjustable example is that I have flown through an area of heavy rain during a stabilized approach. The crew monitored visibility, weather radar and aircraft performance, and remained ready to go around. The rain weakened before landing; otherwise, we would have discontinued the approach.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个可调整的示范答案是，我曾在稳定进近过程中飞经一片大雨区域。机组监控能见度、气象雷达和飞机性能，并随时准备复飞。着陆前雨势减弱；否则我们会中止进近。

cards.audioText: How can heavy rain affect a flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 大雨会如何影响飞行？
cards.referenceText: Heavy rain can reduce visibility, mask terrain or runway cues and increase workload. It may be associated with thunderstorms, turbulence, wind shear, hail and lightning, and it can reduce runway braking performance or increase hydroplaning risk. Very intense precipitation may also affect engines or sensors, so crews should follow limitations and avoid hazardous cells.
cards.referenceTextZh: 大雨会降低能见度、遮蔽地形或跑道目视线索，并增加工作负荷。它可能伴随雷暴、颠簸、风切变、冰雹和闪电，还会降低跑道制动性能或增加滑水风险。极强降水也可能影响发动机或传感器，因此机组应遵守限制并避开危险雷暴单体。

cards.audioText: How do you analyze weather conditions before a flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行前你如何分析天气状况？
cards.referenceText: A model pilot answer would be to review official observations, forecasts, significant-weather products, winds, radar and satellite information before departure. I would compare the route, destination and alternates, then look for trends and operational limits rather than one isolated report. I would update the analysis during the flight and change the plan if the risk increased.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个飞行员示范答案是，起飞前查看官方观测资料、预报、重要天气产品、风、雷达和卫星资料。我会比较航路、目的地和备降场的情况，关注变化趋势和运行限制，而不是只看一份孤立报告。我会在飞行中更新分析，并在风险增加时改变计划。

cards.audioText: Why is understanding adverse weather important for flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 为什么了解不利天气对飞行安全很重要？
cards.referenceText: Adverse weather can change aircraft performance, visibility, runway condition and the crew's available options. Understanding it helps pilots recognize hazards early and make safer decisions about departure, route, approach or diversion. Without that knowledge, normal-looking conditions can develop into a high-workload emergency.
cards.referenceTextZh: 不利天气会改变飞机性能、能见度、跑道状况和机组可用的选择。了解这些影响有助于飞行员及早识别危险，并对起飞、航路、进近或备降作出更安全的决定。缺少这种知识时，看似正常的条件也可能演变成高工作负荷的紧急情况。

cards.audioText: How can adverse weather conditions other than cumulonimbus clouds and turbulence affect flight safety?
cards.audioTextZh: 除积雨云和颠簸外，其他不利天气条件会如何影响飞行安全？
cards.referenceText: Icing can reduce lift and control, fog can remove visual references, and strong winds can affect flight path and runway use. Heavy rain, snow or dust may reduce visibility and contaminate a runway. Extreme temperature can also change performance, equipment reliability and human endurance.
cards.referenceTextZh: 结冰会降低升力和操纵能力，雾会使目视参考消失，强风会影响飞行轨迹和跑道使用。大雨、降雪或沙尘可能降低能见度并污染跑道。极端温度还会改变性能、设备可靠性和人的耐受能力。

cards.audioText: How can strong winds affect an aircraft during flight?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行中，强风会如何影响飞机？
cards.referenceText: Strong winds can cause turbulence, drift, airspeed changes and difficulty maintaining the intended flight path. Near terrain, they may create mountain waves, rotors and strong downdrafts. During takeoff and landing, crosswind, tailwind and gusts can reduce control and performance margins.
cards.referenceTextZh: 强风可能造成颠簸、偏流、空速变化，并使飞机难以保持预定飞行轨迹。在地形附近，强风可能形成山地波、转子气流和强烈下沉气流。起飞和着陆时，侧风、顺风和阵风都会降低操纵与性能裕度。

cards.audioText: Which weather condition do you consider the greatest threat to flight safety, and why?
cards.audioTextZh: 你认为哪种天气条件对飞行安全威胁最大？为什么？
cards.referenceText: One reasonable answer is that severe convective weather presents the greatest overall threat. A thunderstorm can combine turbulence, wind shear, hail, lightning, icing and intense rain in one rapidly changing area. The safest strategy is early avoidance because aircraft capability cannot remove all of those hazards.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合理的回答是，严重对流天气带来的综合威胁最大。雷暴可以在一个迅速变化的区域内同时带来颠簸、风切变、冰雹、闪电、结冰和强降雨。最安全的策略是尽早避开，因为飞机的能力无法消除所有这些危险。

cards.audioText: What measures can reduce the risk of incidents caused by hazardous weather?
cards.audioTextZh: 哪些措施可以降低危险天气引发不安全事件的风险？
cards.referenceText: Risk can be reduced through reliable weather observation and forecasting, thorough briefing and clear operating limits. Pilots need recurrent training, conservative decision-making and updated information from dispatch, ATC and other aircraft. After events, reporting and data review can improve procedures and warning systems.
cards.referenceTextZh: 可靠的天气观测和预报、全面的天气讲解以及明确的运行限制都能降低风险。飞行员需要定期复训、作出保守决定，并持续接收签派、空管和其他飞机提供的最新信息。事件发生后，报告和数据审查可以帮助改进程序与警告系统。

cards.audioText: Where do pilots obtain weather information before departure?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行员在起飞前从哪里获取天气信息？
cards.referenceText: Pilots obtain weather from approved national aviation-weather services, operator or dispatch systems, airport observations and forecasts. Briefings may include radar and satellite products, significant-weather warnings, winds and pilot reports. The crew should know which source is official for the operation and check that the information is current.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员通过经批准的国家航空气象服务、运营人或签派系统、机场观测和预报获取天气信息。天气讲解可能包括雷达和卫星产品、重要天气警告、风和飞行员报告。机组应清楚本次运行以哪个来源为正式依据，并确认信息是最新的。

cards.audioText: Have you ever encountered severe weather during a flight? If so, what happened?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中遇到过恶劣天气吗？如果遇到过，当时发生了什么？
cards.referenceText: A suitable example would be: yes, severe thunderstorms once blocked part of our planned route. The crew detected the weather early, secured the cabin and coordinated a wide deviation with ATC without entering the hazardous cells. The flight remained safe, but the diversion added time and required careful fuel monitoring.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的示范答案是：是的，严重雷暴曾阻断我们计划航路的一部分。机组及早发现天气，确保客舱内人员和物品固定妥当，并与空管协调大范围绕飞，没有进入危险单体。飞行保持安全，但绕飞增加了时间，也要求我们仔细监控燃油。

cards.audioText: What is air density in simple terms?
cards.audioTextZh: 简单来说，什么是空气密度？
cards.referenceText: Air density describes how much mass of air is contained in a given volume. Dense air has more air molecules in that volume, while thin air has fewer. This difference affects how well wings, propellers and engines can perform.
cards.referenceTextZh: 空气密度表示一定体积空气中所含的质量。密度大的空气在相同体积内含有更多空气分子，稀薄空气则更少。这种差异会影响机翼、螺旋桨和发动机的工作性能。

cards.audioText: Why is air density so important for aircraft performance?
cards.audioTextZh: 为什么空气密度对飞机性能如此重要？
cards.referenceText: Aircraft depend on air for lift, engine output and propeller or rotor efficiency. When density decreases, the aircraft generally needs more runway and has less climb performance. Pilots must therefore use performance data that reflects the actual pressure, temperature, altitude and other relevant conditions.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞机依靠空气产生升力，发动机也需要空气提供输出，螺旋桨或旋翼的效率同样受空气影响。密度降低时，飞机通常需要更长跑道，爬升性能也会下降。因此，飞行员必须使用能够反映实际气压、温度、高度和其他相关条件的性能数据。

cards.audioText: What are the three main factors that affect air density?
cards.audioTextZh: 影响空气密度的三个主要因素是什么？
cards.referenceText: The three main factors are atmospheric pressure, temperature and humidity. Lower pressure and higher temperature reduce density. Increasing humidity also reduces density because water vapor is lighter than the dry-air molecules it replaces.
cards.referenceTextZh: 三个主要因素是大气压力、温度和湿度。气压降低和温度升高都会使密度减小。湿度增加也会降低空气密度，因为水汽分子比它所取代的干空气分子轻。

cards.audioText: How does altitude affect air density and aircraft performance?
cards.audioTextZh: 高度如何影响空气密度和飞机性能？
cards.referenceText: As altitude increases, pressure usually falls and the air becomes less dense. Lower density reduces engine, propeller and aerodynamic performance, so takeoff distance can increase and climb rate can decrease. The aircraft performs as if it were operating at the corresponding density altitude.
cards.referenceTextZh: 随着高度增加，气压通常下降，空气也会变得稀薄。密度降低会削弱发动机、螺旋桨和空气动力性能，因此起飞距离可能增加，爬升率可能下降。飞机的性能就像在相应密度高度上运行一样。

cards.audioText: How does temperature affect air density?
cards.audioTextZh: 温度如何影响空气密度？
cards.referenceText: At the same pressure, warmer air is less dense because it expands. Higher temperature therefore raises density altitude and normally reduces takeoff and climb performance. Colder air is denser and generally improves those performance margins, subject to other limitations.
cards.referenceTextZh: 在相同气压下，较暖的空气会膨胀，因此密度更低。温度升高会增加密度高度，通常降低起飞和爬升性能。较冷空气密度更大，一般会改善这些性能裕度，但仍受其他限制约束。

cards.audioText: How does increasing humidity affect air density, and why?
cards.audioTextZh: 湿度增加会如何影响空气密度？为什么？
cards.referenceText: Increasing humidity makes air slightly less dense because water-vapor molecules are lighter than the nitrogen and oxygen they replace. This raises density altitude and can reduce performance. The effect is usually smaller than pressure and temperature effects, but it can add to them on a hot, high day.
cards.referenceTextZh: 湿度增加会使空气密度略微降低，因为水汽分子比它所取代的氮气和氧气分子轻。这会提高密度高度并可能降低性能。其影响通常小于气压和温度的影响，但在高温高原条件下会与它们叠加。

cards.audioText: What does high density altitude mean?
cards.audioTextZh: 高密度高度意味着什么？
cards.referenceText: High density altitude means that the air density is equivalent to the standard atmosphere at a relatively high altitude. In simple terms, the air is thin for the aircraft's actual location. The aircraft will therefore show the reduced performance associated with that higher effective altitude.
cards.referenceTextZh: 高密度高度表示当前空气密度相当于标准大气中一个较高高度的密度。简单地说，对于飞机实际所在位置而言，空气比较稀薄。因此，飞机会表现出与这个较高等效高度相对应的性能下降。

cards.audioText: What performance problems might occur during takeoff in low-density conditions?
cards.audioTextZh: 在低空气密度条件下起飞时，可能出现哪些性能问题？
cards.referenceText: Low-density conditions can increase takeoff distance and reduce acceleration, engine or propeller performance and climb rate. Obstacle clearance may become critical even when the runway appears long enough. A heavily loaded aircraft at a hot, high airport may have very little performance margin.
cards.referenceTextZh: 低空气密度会增加起飞距离，并降低加速性能、发动机或螺旋桨性能以及爬升率。即使跑道看起来足够长，越障能力也可能成为关键限制。载重较大的飞机在高温高原机场可能只剩很小的性能裕度。

cards.audioText: How can a pilot compensate for the effects of low air density?
cards.audioTextZh: 飞行员如何补偿低空气密度带来的影响？
cards.referenceText: The pilot should calculate performance with current conditions and reduce weight or wait for cooler conditions when necessary. A longer suitable runway, a different departure time or a less demanding route may improve the margin. The operation must remain within the aircraft manual and obstacle-clearance requirements; technique cannot create performance that the aircraft does not have.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员应根据当前条件计算性能，必要时减轻重量或等待气温下降。更长且合适的跑道、不同的起飞时间或要求较低的航路都可能增加裕度。运行必须符合飞机手册和越障要求；任何操纵技巧都不能创造飞机本身不具备的性能。

cards.audioText: Can you describe a dangerous situation that could result from ignoring the effects of low air density?
cards.audioTextZh: 你能描述一种忽视低空气密度影响可能造成的危险情况吗？
cards.referenceText: A representative example would be a heavily loaded aircraft departing a hot, high airport without a proper performance calculation. It might use much more runway than expected and then climb too slowly to clear terrain or obstacles. The danger comes from assuming that performance will be the same as on a cool day near sea level.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个有代表性的例子是，载重较大的飞机在高温高原机场起飞前没有正确计算性能。它可能使用远超预期的跑道长度，随后因爬升过慢而无法越过地形或障碍物。危险源于错误地假定飞机性能会与海平面附近的凉爽天气相同。

cards.audioText: What factors should pilots consider during winter operations?
cards.audioTextZh: 冬季运行中，飞行员应考虑哪些因素？
cards.referenceText: Winter planning should cover icing and frost, deicing and holdover time, cold-temperature effects, runway contamination and braking action. Pilots should also consider snow-covered markings, visibility, strong winds, alternate airports and equipment or battery performance. Extra time and a careful preflight inspection are often necessary.
cards.referenceTextZh: 冬季运行计划应涵盖结冰和结霜、除冰与防冰保持时间、低温影响、跑道污染和跑道制动状况。飞行员还应考虑积雪覆盖的标志、能见度、强风、备降机场以及设备或电池性能。通常需要预留更多时间，并认真进行飞行前检查。

cards.audioText: What hazards can pilots face during summer operations?
cards.audioTextZh: 夏季运行中，飞行员可能面临哪些危险？
cards.referenceText: Summer operations can bring thunderstorms, turbulence, wind shear, hail and intense rain. High temperature and high density altitude can reduce takeoff and climb performance, while heat can affect people and equipment. In some regions, smoke, dust or tropical weather may create additional visibility and routing hazards.
cards.referenceTextZh: 夏季运行可能遇到雷暴、颠簸、风切变、冰雹和强降雨。高温和高密度高度会降低起飞与爬升性能，炎热还会影响人员和设备。在某些地区，烟雾、沙尘或热带天气也可能带来额外的能见度和航路危险。

cards.audioText: What emergency equipment is available in the cockpit of the aircraft you fly?
cards.audioTextZh: 你所飞飞机的驾驶舱内配备了哪些应急设备？
cards.referenceText: In a typical transport-aircraft cockpit, emergency equipment includes oxygen masks, smoke goggles, fire extinguishers, life vests and an emergency escape device. The exact equipment and stowage locations depend on the aircraft type. A pilot should use the approved equipment list and cockpit inspection procedure for the aircraft concerned.
cards.referenceTextZh: 典型运输类飞机的驾驶舱应急设备包括氧气面罩、防烟眼镜、灭火器、救生衣和应急逃生装置。具体设备及存放位置取决于机型。飞行员应采用相关飞机经批准的设备清单和驾驶舱检查程序。

cards.audioText: Does the aircraft type you fly have evacuation slides? If so, where are they located?
cards.audioTextZh: 你所飞的机型配有撤离滑梯吗？如果有，安装在哪里？
cards.referenceText: A suitable example would be: the aircraft I fly has evacuation slides at the main passenger doors and at designated emergency exits. Some slides may also serve as flotation devices, depending on the installation. The exact number, type and location must be confirmed from the aircraft's approved emergency-equipment information.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的示范答案是：我所飞机型的主客舱门和指定应急出口配有撤离滑梯。根据安装方式，部分滑梯还可以充当漂浮装置。具体数量、类型和位置必须依据飞机经批准的应急设备资料确认。

cards.audioText: How many evacuation slides are installed on the aircraft type you fly?
cards.audioTextZh: 你所飞的机型安装了多少个撤离滑梯？
cards.referenceText: A suitable example would be: the aircraft variant I fly has six evacuation slides. Four are fitted at the main doors, and two serve the overwing exits. This is a model configuration only, so learners should replace it with the approved number and arrangement for their own aircraft.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的示范答案是：我所飞机型共有六个撤离滑梯。四个安装在主舱门，另外两个用于翼上出口。这只是一个示范构型，学习者应替换为自己所飞机型经批准的数量和布置。

cards.audioText: Under what circumstances should evacuation slides be used?
cards.audioTextZh: 在什么情况下应使用撤离滑梯？
cards.referenceText: Evacuation slides should be used when an armed exit is opened for an emergency evacuation and the height makes an assisted descent necessary. An exit should not be used if fire, obstacles or another hazard makes the outside area unsafe. Cabin crew assess the exit, redirect passengers when necessary and follow the operator's commands and procedures.
cards.referenceTextZh: 当已预位的出口为紧急撤离而打开，并且门槛高度需要辅助下滑时，应使用撤离滑梯。如果出口外有火焰、障碍物或其他危险，就不应使用该出口。客舱机组应评估出口，必要时引导旅客改用其他出口，并遵循运营人的口令和程序。

cards.audioText: Have you ever heard of an evacuation slide being deployed accidentally during ground operations?
cards.audioTextZh: 你听说过地面运行期间撤离滑梯意外释放的情况吗？
cards.referenceText: A suitable example would be: yes, I have heard reports of slides deploying accidentally when a door was opened while still armed. Such an event can injure people near the door and cause significant damage and delay. Good door-status communication and strict use of the operator's arming and disarming procedure help prevent it.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的示范答案是：是的，我听说过舱门仍处于预位状态时被打开，导致滑梯意外释放的事件。这类事件会使舱门附近人员受伤，并造成严重损坏和延误。做好舱门状态沟通，并严格执行运营人的预位和解除预位程序，有助于防止此类事件。

cards.audioText: Why are pilots required to be familiar with emergency equipment?
cards.audioTextZh: 为什么要求飞行员熟悉应急设备？
cards.referenceText: Pilots must be familiar with emergency equipment because an emergency leaves little time to search for instructions or equipment. They need to know what is available, where it is stowed, how to check it and how to use it safely. Regular training also reduces confusion and improves coordination with the cabin crew.
cards.referenceTextZh: 飞行员必须熟悉应急设备，因为紧急情况下没有多少时间查找说明或设备。他们需要知道机上有哪些设备、存放在哪里、如何检查以及怎样安全使用。定期训练还能减少混乱，并改善与客舱机组的协作。

cards.audioText: How easy is the emergency equipment on your aircraft to use?
cards.audioTextZh: 你所飞飞机上的应急设备是否容易使用？
cards.referenceText: A suitable example would be: most emergency equipment on my aircraft is designed for quick use, but it is only easy when the crew has trained with it. Oxygen masks and fire extinguishers require correct handling under stress, and some escape equipment needs careful deployment. Recurrent practice is therefore more important than assuming that the equipment is self-explanatory.
cards.referenceTextZh: 一个合适的示范答案是：我所飞机型的大多数应急设备都便于快速使用，但只有机组接受过训练，操作起来才会真正容易。氧气面罩和灭火器在压力下需要正确操作，有些逃生设备也必须谨慎展开。因此，定期练习比想当然地认为设备一看就会更重要。

cards.audioText: What functions do evacuation slides serve?
cards.audioTextZh: 撤离滑梯有哪些用途？
cards.referenceText: Evacuation slides provide a rapid route from an aircraft exit to the ground when the door sill is high. On some aircraft, certain slides can detach and serve as flotation devices or life rafts. Their exact functions depend on the approved installation, so crews must know the equipment fitted to each aircraft.
cards.referenceTextZh: 当飞机出口门槛较高时，撤离滑梯可以提供一条从出口快速到达地面的通道。在部分飞机上，某些滑梯能够拆下并作为漂浮装置或救生筏使用。具体功能取决于经批准的安装构型，因此机组必须了解每架飞机实际配备的设备。

cards.audioText: Have you ever encountered an emergency, urgency, or distress situation during a flight? If so, what happened?
cards.audioTextZh: 你在飞行中遇到过应急、紧急或遇险情况吗？如果遇到过，当时发生了什么？
cards.referenceText: A suitable example would be: no, I have not encountered a real emergency, urgency or distress situation during a flight. I have practised several emergencies in a simulator, including a loss of cabin pressure followed by oxygen use and an emergency descent. The exercise showed why clear task sharing and checklist discipline are essential.
